before: A saved package could hold two revision annotations with one w:id: the split pieces of a revision someone typed inside, concurrent ids from two peers that met, or a header revision that took a body id.
after: Saving renumbers later duplicates and out-of-range ids in the export snapshot only, so every saved revision annotation has its own w:id across all parts.
reason: The pass runs on the package handed to the serializer and builds new nodes for the export only. The live tree, shared state, operations, journals, and actor id stripes do not change, and saving writes no update to the room. A peer that joins opens bootstrap bytes with export ids and converges with the room's ids when it attaches.
